doc.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005

title: Longevity: diet, vitamins and loving the horn
summary: Al's diet and vitamins, and JoAnn's view that having something you love is key.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Because you are a perfectionist, I can tell. Do you have any words of wisdom for JoAnn and I about longevity. Is there anything you think you’ve done in your life that —

Positively. First of all I’m a fantastic eater. I love all foods. All foods. Name it, all kinds of meats, all kinds of seafood, raw oysters, raw mussels, raw clams. Pomegranates. Fruit. Vegetables. Fish. Three o’clock in the morning I’ll make spaghetti, go to bed, no heartburn. Years ago I’d have heartburn, today I don’t. But I have other obstacles. And I’m a vitamin freak. Always took a lot of vitamins, since 1934 and ’35. And I think that has helped also. A lot of Vitamin E and so forth.
But I think even more than all these things is you have something to do that you love. And I think that’s the whole key to it.
That’s it, the horn. The famous words, “Hey Al are you still playing?” I say, “I am. Only the coffin will take me.”
